It is fixed in the maintained fork github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.0: https://github.com/iskorotkov/avro/security/advisories/GHSA-mc57-h6j3-3hmv, commits https://github.com/iskorotkov/avro/commit/bed99b315ec097a1a5eb7ae074ef57a91848c583 and https://github.com/iskorotkov/avro/commit/e1a570f9a8a4fe4b1bc2b4b1fb6d24e4a5f04358 . The original module github.com/hamba/avro/v2 is archived on GitHub with v2.31.0 as its last release, and the Go vulnerability database lists it as affected in every version with no fix: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5047 . We read every opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository: 23 builds, 0.156.0-r0 to 0.166.0-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64 (46 packages). For each we checked the control section against its index checksum and read the start of the data archive, which holds /usr/bin/otelcol-contrib, up to and including the program's Go build information; that covers its function table (pclntab) and its read-only data, but not the debug sections at the end of the file. A 24th build, 0.166.0-r1, was published on 2026-11-27; we read the start of each of its two packages, and the Go build ID of its program, which ends in a hash of the program content, is the same as that of 0.166.0-r0 on both architectures, so it ships the same program. Each program is a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (the Go release and module versions) and the function names in its function table; runtime.main is present in every build as a control. In 0.156.0-r0 and 0.157.0-r0 the program file table names source files of github.com/hamba/avro/v2@v2.31.0 and the function table holds 559 functions under the github.com/hamba/avro/v2 import path, including (*arrayDecoder).Decode, (*mapDecoder).Decode and (*Reader).ReadBlockHeader: the unfixed release. From 0.158.0-r0 the file table no longer names any github.com/hamba/avro/v2@v2.31.0 source file and the same import path holds 620 functions, in every build on both architectures. The build information shows why: go version -m on 0.157.0-r0 prints dep github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 with no replacement, and on 0.158.0-r0 it prints dep github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 followed by => github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.0, so the code compiled under the hamba import path is the fixed fork release v2.33.0. From 0.158.0-r0 the programs also list github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.1, which is fixed too. The fix commits named above are in the v2.33.0 tag. So 0.156.0-r0 and 0.157.0-r0 are affected, and every build from 0.158.0-r0 is fixed.

The DHI Debian repository lists 23 builds, 0.156.0-0 to 0.166.0-0, for amd64 and arm64 (46 packages). For each we read the control archive, whose file list names only /usr/bin/otelcol-contrib, and the start of the data archive: the Go build ID of /usr/bin/otelcol-contrib, which ends in a hash of the program's content, equals the one in the opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev package for Alpine 3.23 of the same build and architecture (0.156.0-0 and 0.156.0-r0, and so on to 0.166.0-0 and 0.166.0-r0), so each Debian build ships the same program as the Alpine build we read. A 24th build, 0.166.0-1, was published on 2026-11-27: its control archive MD5 checksums and the Go build ID of its program are the same as those of 0.166.0-0 on both amd64 and arm64, so it ships the same program. Each program is a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (the Go release and module versions) and the function names in its function table; runtime.main is present in every build as a control. In 0.156.0-0 and 0.157.0-0 the program file table names source files of github.com/hamba/avro/v2@v2.31.0 and the function table holds 559 functions under the github.com/hamba/avro/v2 import path, including (*arrayDecoder).Decode, (*mapDecoder).Decode and (*Reader).ReadBlockHeader: the unfixed release. From 0.158.0-0 the file table no longer names any github.com/hamba/avro/v2@v2.31.0 source file and the same import path holds 620 functions, in every build on both architectures. The build information shows why: go version -m on 0.157.0-0 prints dep github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 with no replacement, and on 0.158.0-0 it prints dep github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 followed by => github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.0, so the code compiled under the hamba import path is the fixed fork release v2.33.0. From 0.158.0-0 the programs also list github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.1, which is fixed too. The fix commits named above are in the v2.33.0 tag. So 0.156.0-0 and 0.157.0-0 are affected, and every build from 0.158.0-0 is fixed.

For each we read the control archive, whose file list names only /usr/bin/otelcol, and the start of the data archive: the Go build ID of /usr/bin/otelcol, which ends in a hash of the program's content, equals the one in the opentelemetry-collector package for Alpine 3.23 of the same build and architecture (0.156.0-0 and 0.156.0-r0, and so on to 0.166.0-0 and 0.166.0-r0), and so does its MD5 checksum, so each Debian build ships the same program as the Alpine build we downloaded. A 24th build, 0.166.0-1, was published on 2026-11-27: its control archive MD5 checksums and the Go build ID of its program are the same as those of 0.166.0-0 on both amd64 and arm64, so it ships the same program. Each program is a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (the Go release and module versions) and its symbol table; runtime.main is present in every build as a control. Its Go build information lists no github.com/hamba/avro/v2 or github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 module in any build, and no build has a function from either package. The same scan finds Avro decoder functions under the github.com/hamba/avro/v2 import path, such as (*arrayDecoder).Decode and (*Reader).ReadBlockHeader, in every opentelemetry-collector-contrib build. The vulnerable Avro decoder is not part of this package.
